questions.question_text: A car travels $12\,000\text{ km}$ in a year with a fuel consumption rate of $6.5\text{ L}/100\text{ km}$. If fuel costs $\$1.80$ per litre, what is the annual fuel cost?

options.why: Divided by $1000$ instead of $100$ when calculating litres of fuel used.
Omitted dividing distance by $100$ when calculating total fuel consumption.
Calculated only the litres of fuel used and forgot to multiply by the fuel price.

questions.solution_text:
1. **Calculate the annual fuel cost**
$\text{Fuel used} = \frac{12\,000}{100} \times 6.5 = 120 \times 6.5 = 780\text{ L}$
$\text{Fuel cost} = 780 \times \$1.80$
$= \$1404.00$

questions.question_text: A 4WD travels $22\,000\text{ km}$ annually and consumes $8.5\text{ L}/100\text{ km}$. Petrol costs $\$2.00$ per litre. What is the annual fuel expense?

options.why: Calculated fuel litres ($1870\text{ L}$) but forgot to multiply by the price $\$2.00\text{/L}$.
Estimated fuel cost assuming $10\text{ L}/100\text{ km}$ instead of the given $8.5\text{ L}/100\text{ km}$.
Divided by an extra factor of $10$ in the arithmetic.

questions.solution_text:
1. **Calculate the annual fuel cost**
$\text{Fuel used} = \frac{22\,000}{100} \times 8.5 = 220 \times 8.5 = 1870\text{ L}$
$\text{Fuel cost} = 1870 \times \$2.00$
$= \$3740.00$

questions.question_text: Calculate the total annual running cost for a vehicle with annual expenses of: fuel $\$2100$, registration and CTP renewal $\$830$, comprehensive insurance $\$670$, and scheduled servicing $\$500$.

options.why: Omitted the scheduled servicing cost from the annual total.
Omitted the insurance cost from the annual total.
Added registration and CTP twice in the summation.

questions.solution_text:
1. **Sum all recurring annual running costs**
$\text{Total cost} = \$2100 + \$830 + \$670 + \$500$
$= \$4100$

questions.question_text: A car has total annual running costs of $\$4800$ and travels $15\,000\text{ km}$ over the year. What is the running cost per kilometre?

options.why: Divided the distance by total cost instead of dividing cost by distance.
Made an order of magnitude decimal error when dividing by $15\,000$.
Divided by $10\,000\text{ km}$ instead of the actual $15\,000\text{ km}$.

questions.solution_text:
1. **Calculate the rate per kilometre or per time period**
$\text{Cost per km} = \frac{\$4800}{15\,000}$
$= \$0.32\text{/km}$

questions.question_text: A vehicle has an annual running cost of $\$3900$. What is the average weekly cost of running the vehicle ($52$ weeks in a year)?

options.why: Divided by $12$ months instead of $52$ weeks to find weekly cost.
Divided by $60$ instead of $52$ weeks in a year.
Divided by $48$ weeks instead of $52$ weeks.

questions.solution_text:
1. **Calculate the rate per kilometre or per time period**
$\text{Weekly cost} = \frac{\$3900}{52}$
$= \$75.00$

questions.question_text: Two cars both travel $15\,000\text{ km}$ in a year with fuel priced at $\$1.90\text{/L}$. Car 1 uses $9.0\text{ L}/100\text{ km}$ and Car 2 uses $6.0\text{ L}/100\text{ km}$. How much does Car 2 save on fuel over the year?

options.why: Calculated the difference in fuel litres ($450\text{ L}$) without multiplying by the fuel price.
Gave the total fuel cost of Car 2 instead of the savings.
Gave the total fuel cost of Car 1 instead of the savings.

questions.solution_text:
1. **Calculate the annual fuel cost**
$\text{Fuel 1} = 150 \times 9.0 \times \$1.90 = \$2565.00$
$\text{Fuel 2} = 150 \times 6.0 \times \$1.90 = \$1710.00$
2. **Sum all recurring annual running costs**
$\text{Savings} = \$2565.00 - \$1710.00$
$= \$855.00$

questions.question_text: A car is driven $18\,000\text{ km}$ in a year ($7.0\text{ L}/100\text{ km}$, fuel $\$1.90\text{/L}$). Fixed costs are registration $\$790$, comprehensive insurance $\$710$, and two services costing $\$250$ each. What is the total annual running cost?

options.why: Included only one service of $\$250$ instead of two services.
Omitted the servicing costs entirely from the running total.
Added an extra $\$250$ for an unstated third service.

questions.solution_text:
1. **Calculate the annual fuel cost**
$\text{Fuel used} = \frac{18\,000}{100} \times 7.0 = 1260\text{ L}$
$\text{Fuel cost} = 1260 \times \$1.90 = \$2394.00$
2. **Sum all recurring annual running costs**
$\text{Servicing} = 2 \times \$250 = \$500.00$
$\text{Total cost} = \$2394 + \$790 + \$710 + \$500$
$= \$4394.00$

questions.question_text: Car A costs $\$28\,000$ to purchase with annual running costs of $\$4100$. Car B (a fuel-efficient model) costs $\$32\,500$ to purchase with annual running costs of $\$3200$. After how many years of ownership will the total costs (purchase price plus running costs) of the two cars be equal?

options.why: Calculated $\$4500 / \$1100$ incorrectly or rounded down before equality.
Added an extra year after the break-even point instead of finding the equality point.
Divided the purchase price difference by an incorrect estimate of annual savings.

questions.solution_text:
1. **Sum all recurring annual running costs**
$\text{Annual running savings} = \$4100 - \$3200 = \$900$
$\text{Purchase price difference} = \$32\,500 - \$28\,000 = \$4500$
$\text{Years until total costs are equal} = \frac{\$4500}{\$900}$
$= 5\text{ years}$
